'''Grégory Miermont''' (born 16 July 1979) is a French mathematician working on [[probability]], [[random tree]]s and [[random map]]s.

==Biography==
After high school, Miermont trained for two years at [[Classe préparatoire aux grandes écoles]] at the end of which he was admitted at the [[École Normale Supérieure|École normale supérieure]] in Paris. He studied there from 1998 to 2002, spending the 2001–2002 year as a visiting student in [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]]. He received his doctorate at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in 2003, under the supervision of Jean Bertoin. Then, he became a [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] researcher in 2004 at [[University of Paris-Sud]] and [[École Normale Supérieure|École normale supérieure]], and was promoted to the rank of professor in 2009. Since 2012 he is a professor at the [[École Normale Supérieure de Lyon|École normale supérieure de Lyon]].

==Work==
Miermont worked on the theory of [[probability]], more precisely on the geometry and scaling limits of random planar maps, and on fragmentation related to random trees.

==Awards and honors==

===Diplomas, titles and awards===
* 2003: PhD Thesis (advisor J. Bertoin)
* 2008: Habilitation dissertation
* 2007: Prize of the Fondation des Sciences Mathématiques de Paris
* 2009: [[Rollo Davidson Prize]]
* 2012: Prize of the [[European Mathematical Society]]
* 2014: [[Doeblin Prize]][http://www.bernoulli-society.org/index.php/prizes/15-features/169-doeblin-prize-previous-prize-recipients#:~:text=2014%3A%20Gr%C3%A9gory%20Miermont%2C%20ENS%20Lyon,Jason%20Miller%2C%20University%20of%20Cambridge.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201026035856/http://bernoulli-society.org/index.php/prizes/15-features/169-doeblin-prize-previous-prize-recipients#:~:text=2014%3A%20Gr%C3%A9gory%20Miermont%2C%20ENS%20Lyon,Jason%20Miller%2C%20University%20of%20Cambridge. |date=26 October 2020 }}
* 2015: Medallion lecturer: ''Compact Brownian Surfaces''<ref>[http://bulletin.imstat.org/2015/05/medallion-lecture-preview-gregory-miermont/ Medallion Lecture preview – July 2015, Oxford, UK; Grégory Miermont] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150616014556/http://bulletin.imstat.org/2015/05/medallion-lecture-preview-gregory-miermont/ |date=16 June 2015 }}. Retrieved 12 June 2015.</ref>

==Selected writings==
* G. Miermont, Self-similar fragmentations derived from the stable tree. I. Splitting at heights, ''Probab. Theory Related Fields'', 127 (2003), pp.&nbsp;423–454 {{doi|10.1007/s00440-003-0295-x}}.
* B. Haas and G. Miermont, The genealogy of self-similar fragmentations with negative index as a continuum random tree, ''Electron. J. Probab.'', 9 (2004), pp. no. 4, 57–97 {{doi|10.1214/EJP.v9-187}}.
* G. Miermont, Tessellations of random maps of arbitrary genus, ''Ann. Scient. Ec. Norm. Supér.'' 42, fascicule 5, 725–781 (2009). [https://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/AnnalesENS/4_42/html/ens_ann-sc_42_725-781.php URL]
* G. Miermont, "The Brownian map is the scaling limit of uniform random plane quadrangulations". ''Acta Math.'' 210, 319–401 (2013) {{doi|10.1007/s11511-013-0096-8}}.
